title: The Last Vow
premise: Beatrix Thornbury has built a careful life ghostwriting other people's truths, including the memoirs of her charming rival, Julian Ashe — until she discovers both Julian and her estranged first love, Elias Wren, are named on the deed to the Wren family orchard, a vineyard neither can sell without the other. Forced to share a harvest season on the land where they once made promises they broke, Beatrix must choose between finishing Julian's flattering version of history and uncovering what really happened the night the orchard burned. As the vines ripen toward first harvest, old letters surface proving Elias took the blame for a fire Beatrix's father caused, and she realizes loyalty to her family's memory has cost her the only true thing she ever wrote. In the end, she publishes the truth under her own name, signs the deed over as a shared inheritance, and risks her whole heart as Elias presses the season's first cider into her hands.
about_author: Ivo Pemberton is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who spent fifteen years untangling inherited properties in the English countryside before turning to fiction. He writes about love, land, and the documents that bind them from a converted hop barn in Kent.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She delivers chapters of Julian Ashe's glossy memoir to his publisher while hiding behind a nondisclosure agreement thicker than the manuscript itself. Emotional beat: competent isolation — she has made a career of lending pieces of herself and keeping the whole heart locked away.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Sorting her late father's papers, she finds the orchard deed bearing both Elias Wren's name and, shockingly, Julian's — an inheritance clause neither man seems to know about. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity; the past tense of her life just became present.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He arrives at Thornbury Orchard intending to buy out his co-owner and leave, only to find Beatrix standing in the doorway of the house he was raised beside. Emotional beat: guarded recognition, twelve years of silence collapsing into one awkward handshake.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She proposes they run the season together and split proceeds rather than litigate, hiding that she's also drafting Julian's memoir nearby. Emotional beat: negotiation as armor — every practical term is a wall against feeling.

chapters.title: Julian Calls Collect
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Charming and entitled, he pressures Beatrix to finish his memoir fast and dismisses the orchard as 'a tax nuisance,' hinting he knows more about the fire than he's said. Emotional beat: unease; the rival's polish begins to look like lacquer over rot.

chapters.title: Pruning What Grows Back
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Working the vines side by side, he and Beatrix fall into old rhythms — her laughing at his terrible pruning, him remembering why he loved her. Emotional beat: warmth sneaking past defenses, immediately regretted.

chapters.title: The Burn Scar
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She finds the charred corner of the orchard her father never replanted and recalls the night of the fire, when seventeen-year-old Elias confessed to it and vanished from her life. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, loyalty to her father's memory hardening like scar tissue.

chapters.title: Rain on the Tin Roof
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Storm traps them in the packing shed; almost-kiss interrupted by Beatrix retreating behind work talk. Emotional beat: longing and self-punishment — Elias still believes he owes her distance for what he 'did.'

chapters.title: Chapters for Sale
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. He visits the orchard unannounced, performs magnanimity, and privately instructs his lawyer to force a sale before harvest. Emotional beat: menace under charm; the reader sees what Beatrix won't.

chapters.title: The Ledger Her Father Kept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the farmhouse attic she finds her father's old ledger with entries suggesting insurance fraud around the fire — and a page torn out. Emotional beat: vertigo; the loyal daughter begins auditing her own inheritance.

chapters.title: First Budbreak
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A tender scene teaching Beatrix to graft; they speak honestly about the years apart without touching the fire. Emotional beat: fragile hope, the first chapter written in present tense instead of past.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She matches handwriting in the ledger to Julian's teenage hand — Julian witnessed the fire and was paid by her father to stay quiet. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding; her two inheritances, the memoir and the orchard, are the same lie.

chapters.title: What Elias Confessed To
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback chapter: young Elias took the blame because Beatrix's father begged him to, promising to fund his mother's medical debts — a debt of loyalty that cost him Beatrix. Emotional beat: tragic nobility revealed as coercion.

chapters.title: Deadline in the Vine Rows
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Julian's lawyer serves partition papers demanding sale before harvest; Beatrix must finish the memoir that will canonize the lie or blow up her career. Emotional beat: cornered — loyalty vs. truth becomes literal paperwork.

chapters.title: The Night Both Names Were Signed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They discover the deed's odd clause: their fathers co-signed it the week after the fire, binding the families together deliberately — perhaps as penance. Emotional beat: awe; the stubborn document was an apology all along.

chapters.title: Confession at the Press House
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She tells Elias what she found in the ledger; he admits what he traded his name for. Anger, then something quieter. Emotional beat: truth as excavation — painful, but the ground is finally clear for planting.

chapters.title: The Memoir She Won't Write
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She burns her draft of Julian's final chapters and emails the publisher a resignation that names herself as author of what comes next. Emotional beat: terrifying liberation; the ghostwriter chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve Sabotage
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Desperate, Julian tampers with the press equipment and confronts Beatrix, revealing his full knowledge of the fire and daring her to prove it. Emotional beat: climax of villainy; the mask fully off.

chapters.title: The First Pressing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Harvest day: the community gathers, the sabotaged press is repaired with Elias's grandfather's spare parts, and the first juice runs gold while Julian's lawyer arrives with an injunction — and Beatrix counters with the ledger. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively; the vow fulfilled not in words but in work.

chapters.title: Truth, Bylined
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She publishes an account of the fire under her own name; Julian settles rather than face court, ceding his deed share. Emotional beat: reckoning and release — loyalty to truth finally outranks loyalty to blood and brand.

chapters.title: The Second Vow
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under the replanted burn scar, now budding, Elias asks Beatrix to stay — not as penance or partnership but as choice. She says yes with her whole heart, no pieces lent. Emotional beat: vulnerable joy; love in present tense.

chapters.title: Cider and Signatures
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue. One year later: first bottled vintage labeled 'Last Vow,' a new deed with both names held jointly, her published book on the farmhouse table. Emotional beat: resolution — memory honored, inheritance shared, truth kept like a good vine, pruned and tended.
